newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down vs US dollar on intervention.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down vs US dollar on intervention.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.3030 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday from Monday's 8.3024, ending a run of rises over six straight trading sessions on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, dealers said.
They said central bank intervention was the main reason for today's fall.

The yuan opened slightly up at 8.3021 and moved in the range of 8.3018 and 8.3023 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.3014 before falling in the last fifteen minutes and hitting a low of 8.3035 just before the close.
Trading was more active than that of the past few days, with most done at 8.3020, traders said.

"It was clear that the People's Bank of China depressed the yuan later in the session to halt its quick rise," said one dealer. "The intervention weakened the strong pro-yuan sentiment to some extent."
"Technically a correction was needed after consecutive rises," a second dealer said.
Dealers expect the yuan to move up slightly to 8.3020 on Wednesday.
The yuan ended down at 7.5825 from 7.5400 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0734 from 1.0736 against the Hong Kong dollar.
